brief: NVDA's Board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO this morning, a move Wolfe says the Trump Administration orchestrated, with the President discussing his involvement on TV. The Board cited input from senior US government levels in concluding reinstatement poses no national security risk. Huang's return restores strategic vision, expertise, relationships and morale. Administration backing, a continuing Board probe into Huang being targeted by foreign intelligence, a new National Security and Export Control Committee, and a planned Chief Compliance Officer hire should calm fears over alleged improper China sales, though Wolfe notes no evidence of violation has surfaced and still expects a Congressional inquiry from the incoming Democrats. Wolfe's own view is demand so far exceeds supply, so NVDA had no reason to ship where prohibited. On new SE Asia and Brazil data center export controls in effect since last week, Wolfe wants more geographic and customer-HQ revenue disclosure as the key investor reassurance, while NVDA says any impact is insignificant given supply constraints. Wolfe also expects continued financing-deal scrutiny despite the reinstatement, views CEO-CFO tension there as healthy, and sees the financing, like AVGO's, as short-term until neocloud and frontier-model customers mature. Wolfe keeps Outperform, $200 target, 59.3% upside from $125.53.
